main.definition: miso-57 KEEPER-CANDIDATE (recommended to owner 2026-07-12; keeper stays miso-56 pending decision): the miso-56 keeper recipe replayed from its exhaustive meta.json (strict replay -- errors on unmapped keys) with exactly two structural transmission changes on the FINDING SS10 pointer-1 lane (RDT S->N congestion depth, the largest quantified 2025 lead): (1) South-seam external-zone split (miso_south_seam_split) -- the shared MISO_external bus linked to all five border zones, letting the LP wheel South energy South->external->Midwest around the RDT contract path for free (2025 diagnostic: 1,255 MW summer-mean bypass while the RDT S->N link carried 54 MW); the southern neighbors (SOCO/TVA/AECI) are electrically south of the RDT, so the South seam now lands on its own MISO_external_South zone. (2) Published RDT operating representation (miso_rdt_tcdc) -- the static JOA contract caps (3,000 N->S / 2,500 S->N) become the 92% default derate as the free tier ('MISO derates the RDT limit to 92 percent of the contract limit by default', 2024 SOM SSIII.B) plus the published two-step TCDC ($40/MWh at the modeled limit, $500/MWh from 102% of it, hard bound at the JOA contract entitlement) as priced one-way tiers. Zero fitted scalars; all parameters published (constants.MISO_RDT_*; MISO-SPP JOA / FERC accession 20151013-5444). Mechanism verification: RDT S->N carries 1,139/1,035 MW mean in 2023/24 vs measured 917/1,108 (2023/2024 SOM), binds at the derated 2,300 MW in ~25% of hours vs the IMM's 'more than one quarter of RT intervals' (2024), and 2024 gains the model's first DA >$200 tail hours (Aug-26 HE15/17/18, Midwest-wide with South decoupled below -- RDT congestion price formation). Score flat-to-marginally-better on the same-basis re-score of miso-56 (C2-2025 gas -11.0->-10.1 / coal +8.8->+7.6, C3a-2024 -3.3->-3.0, C3c-2024 0->3 h, C1 rows within +/-0.4 TWh, C5a in commercial band both). C3a-2025 -13.3% flat: the model's 2025 RDT direction is INVERTED vs measured (N->S-dominant vs the IMM's S->N-dominant summer; Jun-Aug Midwest-South separation +$0.02 vs measured $9.31/MWh) -- pinning the residual 2025 gap on the Midwest supply-cost gradient (COAL_BIT/CC mid-merit split + import under-run lane), not the transmission representation.
main.market_story: Zero-forcing twin near-identical (CT_PEAKER +0.6/+0.28/+0.47 TWh 2023/24/25, COAL_PRB -0.25/-0.29/-0.22, all others <0.25 TWh): the only binding merchant floor remains the CT evening reliability deployment (real MISO RA/LOLE-driven evening commitment). The RDT/topology mechanisms are market structure, stay armed in the twin, and carry their flows economically.
